stem:
Ritu studies the diagram of right-angled triangles $PQR$ and $XYZ$, each with a right angle marked. The hypotenuses $QR$ and $YZ$ are equal, and legs $PQ$ and $XY$ are equal.

Which claim correctly decides congruence?

options.text: Call the triangles congruent even when either triangle need not be right-angled.
Say the same RHS match also settles congruence for non-right SSA pairs in general.
The triangles are congruent by RHS: right angle, equal hypotenuses, and one equal corresponding leg.
Require two equal angles and the included side (ASA) before congruence can be decided here.

teacher.key_rationale: RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, and one other corresponding side guarantee congruence for right triangles. Dropping the right-angle requirement omits a condition. Extending RHS to general non-right SSA over-scopes. Demanding ASA conflates another criterion.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as two right triangles PQR and XYZ with equal hypotenuses and one equal leg marked.
